title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: federated connectors can create, update and delete in third-party systems
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents preview Graph automation for publisher-type access and user access, which the briefing incorrectly calls undocumented. The roadmap, licensing and admin paths are supported; the claim that the confirmation card explains cancellation remains unconfirmed.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Publisher-provided create, update and delete tools are now usable from Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: When a connector provides the appropriate tools, users can ask Microsoft 365 Copilot to create, update, or delete information in a connected third-party system on their behalf.
claims.fix: Add after the first paragraph of What's changing: 'The general Copilot connectors overview still describes federated connectors as read-only, alongside a note that write actions start in early October 2026; this briefing follows the launched roadmap item and the feature-specific federated connectors overview.' The conflicting page is https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview.

claims.where: What's changing: Until October 2026
claims.claim: Federated connectors were read-only before October 2026.
claims.quote:
Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

- Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph
claims.claim: Federated Copilot connectors use Model Context Protocol.
claims.quote: Use Model Context Protocol (MCP) to fetch data in real time.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph
claims.claim: Federated connectors query third-party services in real time.
claims.quote: Federated connectors use MCP to access data in real time, so Copilot can retrieve up-to-date information directly from external systems.

claims.where: What's changing: first and second paragraphs; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: No data is indexed into Microsoft 365. Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: Actions run with the user's own account and permissions in the third-party service.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions. Copilot can change only what the user is already permitted to change in the source system.

claims.where: What's changing: the roadmap item says every action requires confirmation
claims.claim: The roadmap says every create, update or delete action requires explicit user confirmation before it runs.
claims.quote: every create, update, or delete action requires the user's explicit confirmation before it runs.

claims.where: What's changing: Needs approval; summary
claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools default to Needs approval.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools default to Needs approval, which means Copilot asks for confirmation each time.

claims.where: What's changing: confirmation card; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The confirmation card lets users review the parameters to be sent.
claims.quote: Users can expand the card to review the action parameters before approving it.

claims.where: What's changing: nothing is transmitted
claims.claim: While an action awaits confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.
claims.quote: While an action is awaiting confirmation, nothing is sent to the connected system until the user responds.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow once; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Allow once runs the action and asks again for the next use of the tool.
claims.quote: Allow once | Runs the action now. Copilot asks again the next time it wants to use the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Allow for conversation
claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses later approval prompts for the same tool in that conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: What's changing: Always allow; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Always allow suppresses later prompts for the user's tool without a time expiry, subject to revocation or tool changes.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.where: What's changing: Cancel; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Cancel declines the action and leaves the connected system unchanged.
claims.quote: Cancel | Declines the action. Nothing is changed in the connected system.

claims.where: What's changing: per tool; Governance controls
claims.claim: Reusable approval choices apply to an individual tool, not the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.where: What's changing: publisher adds or changes a tool
claims.claim: A new or changed write-capable tool is set to Needs approval.
claims.quote: If a connector publisher adds a new write-capable tool or changes an existing one, the tool is set to Needs approval by default.

claims.where: What's changing: revocable in Settings; Governance controls: user-side tool approvals
claims.claim: Users manage or reset tool approvals in Copilot Settings > Sources > connector > Tools > Write/Delete tools.
claims.quote: Users can review or reset tool permissions in Copilot by going to Settings > Sources and selecting the connector. The Tools section groups the connector's Write/Delete tools separately from its Read tools.

claims.where: What's changing: the roadmap item says administrators can view tools
claims.claim: The roadmap says administrators can view read and write/delete tools and disable connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can view each connector's read and write/delete tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and disable connectors that don't meet their organization's policies.

claims.quote: Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
Agents

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: admin-published connectors
claims.claim: Admin-published federated connectors can create, update or delete where tools provide those actions, with user approval and source permissions.
claims.quote: Admin-published FCCs can also create, update, or delete data where the connector provides those tools, with the user's approval and subject to their permissions in the source system.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: supported actions vary
claims.claim: Supported admin-published connector actions vary by connector.
claims.quote: Supported actions vary by connector.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance controls: Purview audit
claims.claim: Administrators can audit federated connector activity in Microsoft Purview.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.where: Why it matters: export Customer Data; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Write actions export Customer Data to the connected system.
claims.quote: These actions export Customer Data to the connected system to create, update, delete, or otherwise modify data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Write payloads can carry conversation content, including Microsoft 365 content, to the third-party system.
claims.quote:
a user can turn an escalation email into an issue in a project-tracking tool
Copilot sends the connector the information it needs to complete the action and returns the outcome to the user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The source system enforces permissions, so a user cannot write data they lack permission to change directly.
claims.quote: The source system enforces all permissions. Users can only access content they're authorized to view and make changes they're authorized to make in the original data source.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Federated connector access uses the user's OAuth connection to the source service.
claims.quote: An OAuth-based identity configuration between the external service and Microsoft Entra ID, so Copilot can query the source on behalf of the signed-in user.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: MCP servers restricting inbound source IPs need to allow Microsoft's static egress IP addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, configure its firewall to allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Copilot selects relevant connector tools dynamically.
claims.quote: When appropriate, Microsoft 365 Copilot dynamically selects relevant tools to retrieve information or perform an action.
